collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a craftsperson or another adult; in the story (name1) has thick, tightly coiled hair)

collection.description: A villager with thick coiled hair has snapped a third fine-toothed comb: carve a wide-toothed comb, or help get the comb out.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has a great cloud of thick, tightly coiled hair, and (subject.he/she) loves it. What (subject.he/she) does not love is combs. Every comb in the village was made with fine, close teeth for straight or wavy hair, and (subject) has just snapped the third one this month, halfway through. (subject.He/she) is standing outside (subject.his/her) hut with a comb stuck in (subject.his/her) hair and a look of deep suffering. (friend), who carves combs, walks by.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: First things first. (friend) carefully works the broken comb out, tooth by tooth, while (subject) sits on the step and complains about every comb ever made. It takes a long time. "Who carves these?" asks (subject), finally. (friend) clears (friend.his/her) throat. "I do." There's a long pause. "Well," says (subject), "you can carve me a better one." (friend) does.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (friend) looks at the broken comb, looks at (subject)'s hair, and says, "Ah. Wrong comb." (friend.He/she) comes back that evening with a new one carved from hard dark wood: long, strong, widely spaced teeth. It slides through (subject)'s hair like a fish through water. (subject) closes (subject.his/her) eyes in bliss. (friend) is soon carving them for half the village.
